findings.issue: Spurious syllables きごう inserted into the phonetic transcription: the whitespace token was annotated with reading きごう (記号 'symbol') and it leaked into the kana. The sentence reads あめがふっているけれども + でかけます with nothing in between.
findings.current: あめがふっているけれどもきごうでかけます
findings.suggested: あめがふっているけれどもでかけます

findings.issue: Same artifact as the kana: 'kigou' (reading assigned to a whitespace token) is embedded in the romanization. Not covered by the known punctuation/katakana issue.
Token whose surface is a single space carries the reading きごう ('symbol' label leaked in as a reading). A space has no reading; this is the root cause of the corrupted kana/romaji.
findings.suggested: null (no reading; ideally drop the whitespace token entirely)

findings.issue: Generated Japanese contains a stray space between けれども and 出かけます; Japanese text should have no internal space here.
findings.current: 雨が降っているけれども 出かけます
findings.suggested: 雨が降っているけれども出かけます

findings.issue: 'Well, I'm off' reads as announcing one's departure (≈私は行くよ), losing the exhaustive-listing が nuance of volunteering ('I'm the one who'll go') that expl_en/expl_pt and the pt translation ('Então eu vou') explicitly teach.

Literal field fails to mirror the structure: 私が (marked subject) and final よ are not reflected, and 'I'm off' repeats the departure misreading. lit_pt correctly mirrors ('eu (sujeito) vou, viu'); lit_en should match it.
findings.suggested: Well then, I (subject) will go, you know.
